free_tier.stated: Regular account: 50 GB storage, 100 KB/s download, next download only after a 1-hour delay, no simultaneous downloads, no direct downloads, files deleted 60 days after the last download.
free_tier.notes: The free column also allows remote URL and FTP upload: no.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated on the payments page; the FAQ was not opened

retention.stated: Regular: '60 days after last download'. Premium: 'Unlimited'.

egress.terms: Premium: 'Download speed: Unlimited', 'Simultaneous downloads: Yes', 'Direct downloads: Yes'. Regular: 100 KB/s, one at a time, one hour between downloads. No byte allowance is published on either column.

interface_detail: Web upload, remote URL upload and FTP upload on premium. The site is an XFileSharing-style host, which normally exposes an API module, but no endpoint was found or read here.
tooling: FTP upload on premium is the only non-browser path stated. No rclone backend. The host is on both the PrimeLeech and Leechall generator lists, so a leecher can pull from it without a premium account.
chaining: A 500 GB premium host at $15.95 a month, priced per 30 days rather than per byte, with 330 days at $117.95 the cheapest per day. Useful as a redirect target for a release the debrids do not cache.

limits.value: 500 GB storage on premium, 50 GB on regular
100 KB/s and a 1-hour wait between downloads on the regular account
regular files deleted 60 days after the last download

limits_note: The storage figure is a stored-byte ceiling, not a transfer allowance; the transfer side is only shaped (100 KB/s), never metered.
binding_note: On premium the throttle is removed and the 500 GB storage ceiling becomes the next wall.

identity_cost.detail: Payments listed as 'Bank Cards | PayPaI | Bitcoin | Ethereum'. The site also shows a WebMoney passport identifier (411266485536), which is a payment-processor identity rather than a signup requirement.

reliability_note: The 1-hour wait and the 100 KB/s cap are on the account, not the file, so a batch of small files on the free tier takes a day in queue time alone.
confidence_note: Feature and price table read on the vendor payments page. Because this is an XFileSharing-derived host, a per-file upload cap almost certainly exists and is not in this record; the FAQ page would supply it.

evidence.proved: the Premium/Regular comparison (500 GB vs 50 GB storage, unlimited vs 100 KB/s, unlimited vs 60-day retention) and the prices 15.95 USD / 30 days, 39.95 / 90 days, 117.95 / 330 days

price_per_tb_month: USD 15.95 per 30 days for 500 GB stored
notes: Cheapest per day is the 330-day plan at USD 0.357/day against USD 0.532/day for the 30-day. Nothing here prices transfer, so a client storing 500 GB and pulling it monthly is paying for storage only.

extras.plans: 15.95 USD 30 days; 39.95 USD 90 days; 117.95 USD 330 days
